title: Increase in Postal Rates despite Profitability Recorded by SingPost
what_it_is: Increase in Postal Rates despite Profitability Recorded by SingPost

sections.label: Postage increase impact on households
sections.summary: Corporate entities bear most of the impact as they send 80% of letter mail, but all households get 10 stamps of 51 cents each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The impact will be felt mostly by corporate entities rather than households, as they account for 80% of all letter mail sent in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Nonetheless, all households will receive a booklet of 10 stamps of 51-cent each, which is enough to cover the increase in postage fees for the average household for about a year.

sections.label: SingPost core business losses
sections.summary: SingPost's core post and parcel business in Singapore incurred operating losses of $16 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: SingPost’s core business in Singapore is post and parcel, which incurred operating losses of $16 million.

sections.label: IMDA approves postage rate increase
sections.summary: The Infocomm Media Development Agency approved SingPost's request to raise postage rates to better reflect letter delivery costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The Infocomm Media Development Agency (IMDA) approved SingPost’s request to raise postage rates to better reflect the cost of delivering letters.

sections.label: Government review of postal future
sections.summary: The Government is carrying out a fundamental review on the future of post and longer-term sector considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: First, the Government is carrying out a fundamental review on the future of post and the longer-term considerations around this sector, as well as changes to the postal landscape in the coming years.

sections.label: SingPost reviews costs and operations
sections.summary: SingPost has committed to reviewing its costs and operations as part of its business transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: SingPost has committed to reviewing its costs and operations as part of its business transformation.

sections.label: Cross-subsidisation not sustainable for SingPost
sections.summary: It is not sustainable for a publicly listed company to sustain a loss-making business, as most of SingPost's revenue and profits come from outside Singapore and unregulated businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Second, on the Member's question about cross-subsidisation, we have to understand that it is not sustainable for a publicly listed company to sustain a loss-making business, especially for SingPost where the bulk of its revenue is from outside of Singapore and more than 90% of its profits are from unregulated businesses.

sections.label: Ringfenced domestic regulated segment revenue
sections.summary: Revenue and profits are ringfenced for the domestic regulated segment and are not to offset losses in other businesses or vice versa.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The revenue, the profits, are ringfenced for the domestic regulated segment; they are not supposed to offset losses in its other businesses and vice versa.
